Findings.Title: Successful artifact reviews discard the required missing-metric diagnostic
Findings.Defect: The worker produces token_metadata_unavailable when the CLI omits token counts, but CompleteHostileReviewAttemptCommand persists Outcome.diagnostics only in its failure branch. Its success branch and activity write the execution and accepted result without diagnostic rows. A successful review can therefore omit metrics without the diagnostic the unchanged stored criterion requires.
Findings.Evidence: Contract counterexample, not executed product code: a reviewer exits successfully with valid actual model/effort and a valid verdict, but the CLI supplies no input/output token counts. Section 16.7 makes both values null and adds token_metadata_unavailable. Complete takes success at line 1753/1766; no unit stores that diagnostic. The stored FR criterion 3 requires unavailable metrics to be omitted with a diagnostic. The new metadata test name at 1663 promises this outcome but the handler contract does not produce it.
Findings.ChangeToPass: Persist sanitized Outcome.diagnostics for every accepted completion outcome, independently of success/failure/cancellation, inside the same fenced audited transaction. Keep duplicate or stale completion side effects prohibited. Propagate to the Complete activity and metadata contract. Strengthen HostileReviewExecutionMetadataFromProvenanceMissingTokensDiagnosed to cover successful reviews as well as failures and cancellations; amend TEST-MCP-HOSTILEREVIEW-003 in H0 only after approval, with mocks green before H3 production binding, as D-09 requires.

Findings.Title: A fast artifact-review exit with missing provenance has no consistent execution-identity path
Findings.Defect: The added missing-provenance failure forbids an execution row and puts the launch identity in a diagnostic, but the canonical DTO, field writers and relationship still promise one execution per launched process. For an exit before first renewal, Complete writes Attempt.ExecutionId only when Outcome.execution is set, and that same branch always writes the execution row. There is no declared representation that both honors the no-row rule and sets the promised attempt identity.
Findings.Evidence: Contract counterexample: an adapter has a provenance source and launches, but a short run exits before RenewalInterval with no readable actual model or effort. The pre-launch guard cannot catch this history. Line 1655 explicitly selects runtime_identity_unavailable with no execution row. Leaving Outcome.execution null skips both the row and Attempt.ExecutionId at 1753; supplying metadata creates the forbidden row and cannot truthfully supply mandatory actual model/effort. The failure activity at 1769 instead says record the execution whenever a process started. B.9 labels the relationship one per launched process. The ID in a diagnostic is useful evidence but is not the specified writer of Attempt.ExecutionId.
Findings.ChangeToPass: Define one canonical representation for launched-but-unverifiable execution. Separate the observed launch identity and times from optional validated provenance, or explicitly specify an equivalent non-fabricating contract. Give fast completion an independent writer for Attempt.ExecutionId; state consistently whether an execution row is absent and how that exception relates to the nullable relationship. Update the DTO, producer, Complete activity, storage prose and B.9. Extend HostileReviewFastExitRecordsExecutionAndTerminalFields with launch-then-missing-provenance before the first renewal, and retain truthful diagnostics. Record the named cases on the existing TEST in approved H0, bind in H3; no new operator policy is needed.

Findings.Title: The first output append bypasses refusal handling in the worker activity
Findings.Defect: RunReviewerProcess sends the initial hv_brief AppendHvRunOutputCommand directly to StreamReviewerOutput on an unconditional edge. No outcome dispatch connects that initial call to the required stale-fence stop, audit stop, corrupt/malformed/non-retryable failure, or same-sequence retry. The start and final-flush calls also omit their retryable-conflict branches. Correct universal prose at 1518 does not make this purported complete activity consistent.
Findings.Evidence: Contract counterexample: RecordHvRunStart succeeds; the sequence-1 append refuses with audit_unavailable, evidence_corrupt, validation_error or non-retryable conflict. At 1538 the only edge enters streaming, even though 1518 requires killing the process and either stopping without writes or invoking FailAttempt. With a refused first batch, proceeding to later sequences can also create an absent first chunk. The repair correctly funnels Fail calls through FailAttempt and fixes the host/finalizer branches; it still does not dispatch every outcome of the calls that lead to them. R3-F05 explicitly rejected generic prose beside unconditional activity edges and required this propagation class to be fixed.
Findings.ChangeToPass: Use a canonical nested append-result activity at initial, timed/size, and final flushes, or draw every outcome at each call. Advance only after appended; retry the same sequence on retryable conflict; kill and stop on stale/audit refusal; kill then FailAttempt on corruption, malformed input or non-retryable conflict. Show retryable start/heartbeat outcomes consistently. Strengthen existing named worker refusal/output-integrity tests to inject each refusal at sequence 1 and the final flush, with H0 mocks and H3 production binding; surface checks remain in the phases where their dependencies exist.

Findings.Title: Claim-time reassignment promises capacity filtering that the canonical round-robin policy cannot perform
Findings.Defect: ClaimHvRunCommand asks RoundRobinAssignment for an eligible reviewer with free capacity, but HvReviewerEligibility deliberately excludes capacity and RoundRobinAssignment selects and advances the cursor for the first eligible reviewer. Its only inputs are submitter/author identity, and its only refusal is no eligible reviewer. It has no claim-time candidate predicate or capacity branch. The caller and canonical shared policy specify different selections.
Findings.Evidence: Contract counterexample: a queued request loses its assignee to Offline. After the cursor, reviewer A is Online and eligible but at MaxConcurrentRuns; later reviewer B is Online, eligible and free. RoundRobinAssignment at 1343/1352 returns A and writes its cursor. Claim at 962/978 promises B or a truthful no-capacity result. Starting A exceeds capacity; rejecting A and rolling back can choose A again on every poll and starve B, especially because A has no review time limit. Repeated committed cursor skips are another unspecified algorithm and contradict null/writes-nothing at 962. SerializableWrite provides isolation but does not supply the missing selection rule.
Findings.ChangeToPass: Define capacity-aware claim reassignment in the one canonical round-robin contract, with an explicit mode or caller-provided candidate filter, and atomically recheck capacity with the claim. Preserve admission eligibility and admission while all reviewers are busy. Specify cursor/request behavior when no capacity exists. Propagate the unit, policy, activity and test catalog. Add named cases to existing FR/TR/TEST-MCP-HVPIPE-002 or -007 for skipping a full eligible reviewer when a later one is free, and all-full with no spurious write; H0 mocks, H3 production.
